Hi Akira — thanks, and great question.

Short answer: we'll send calendar invites with explicit timezone metadata (Asia/Singapore and Asia/Tokyo labels) and also include local times in the body so everyone sees the expected clock time. Important note on the specific slot you suggested:

- Tue Mar 22 23:00 SGT = Wed Mar 23 00:00 JST (so in Tokyo the calendar will show the meeting as the next calendar day).
- For Sydney (AEDT) on that date it would be Wed Mar 23 01:00 AEDT — note Australia DST often changes in April, but on Mar 23 it is still AEDT (UTC+11).

To avoid next-day confusion, would you prefer we:
1) Keep the 23:00 SGT slot and label the invite as "Wed Mar 23 — 00:00 JST / 23:00 SGT" so Tokyo sees the correct next-day date, or
2) Move it earlier to Wed Mar 23 09:00 SGT (10:00 JST / 11:00 AEDT) which keeps it in the same local business day for everyone?

I've attached a draft invite and a short mutual action plan. If you confirm option 1, we'll send one invite with explicit TZ tags; if option 2, we'll send an updated invite in SGT and JST that displays the same calendar date for everyone.

Attachments: redwood-demo-invite-TOKYO.ics (draft), mutual-action-plan.docx

Best,
